Synopsis:
Iran has expanded its blacklist of non-compliant vessels barred from the Strait of Hormuz to 56 ships, up from 45 announced on August 24. The list covers a wide range of tanker types including VLCCs, LNG and LPG carriers, and clean product vessels. Iran threatens fines, confiscation or detention for listed ships, and warns that vessels cooperating with them via STS transfers will also be blacklisted. The move is set against a backdrop of an ongoing war triggered by US and Israeli strikes on Iran, which has already dramatically reduced traffic through the strait — previously handling ~20% of global oil and LNG flows. Major downstream buyers including Indian refiners and a global energy major are already avoiding listed vessels. The US has sanctioned the PGSA, creating further legal complexity for any engagement.

Q01. Is the content relevant to gas in terms of low supply, high demand, market crisis, physical issues? How severe is the issue?
Relevance: YES — LNG and LPG tankers are explicitly named on the blacklist; the Strait of Hormuz handled ~20% of global LNG flows pre-war, now reduced to a trickle, directly threatening supply availability.
